concepts.name: 01-swept-f
concepts.title: Swept F
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: original Flight Deck logo exploration, second round.
Primary request: Create one original aviation-adjacent abstract logo for the project "Flight Deck", inspired by the user's two visual references.
Reference cues: The first reference is a solid black, horizontally swept symbol with a broad nearly level upper edge, a diagonal left shoulder, pointed right tip, and a lower curved blade divided by a rising white airflow channel. The second reference is a compact circular blue/red mark with a diagonal ascending arrowlike stroke, a returning outer arc, and large teardrop-shaped negative-space openings. These are inspiration for curves, directional energy and cutouts. Develop a distinct new silhouette.
Presentation: square pure white canvas, one large solid black mark centered above the exact text "Flight Deck" in a restrained medium-weight modern sans serif. Spacious layout, mark about half the canvas width, generous gap above the wordmark. No concept name or extra text.
Style: flat, crisp vector-like logo graphic, minimal substantial shapes with smooth deliberate curves and sharp tapered terminals. Render black and white only, no gradients, shadows, textures, mockups, borders or decorative lines. This is a raster concept with vector-friendly geometry.
Requirements: a compact memorable silhouette, bold enough for small icons, open negative spaces. Suggest aviation through banking, lift and airflow. Avoid literal airplanes, birds, feathers, fuselages, generic paper-plane icons and stock arrow-in-circle symbols.
Specific concept: SWEPT F. An original abstract F built from two broad forward-swept airfoil shapes. Its upper shape has a restrained near-horizontal roof and a generous curved descending left stem; its shorter middle arm rises toward a sharp upper-right terminal. One clean tapered white channel separates the arms and opens to the right. The silhouette is compact, approximately 1.15 times wider than tall, with a readable but subtle F structure. Emphasize the contrast between a taut outer edge and a deeply scooped inner curve. Do not simply redraw the first reference: give this mark a substantial curved left stem, shorter upper reach, and a more upright, balanced F silhouette.

concepts.name: 02-orbital-climb
concepts.title: Orbital climb

Specific concept: ORBITAL CLIMB. A single broad sculpted ribbon makes an asymmetric three-quarter circular banking turn and then sweeps diagonally upward to a fine terminal at about one o'clock. The circular shape is open at the upper right, not enclosed in a separate ring. The interior negative space is a generous rounded triangular aperture with a curved side. Vary the band weight from broad lower-left mass to a taut narrow rising upper-right tip. Overall footprint nearly square. The ascent should be implied by the ribbon's taper, not a conventional triangular arrowhead. Bold continuous silhouette with one large white opening. No separate blade crossing the ring, no lowercase a or at-sign, no duplicated loops. Capture the second reference's compact rotational energy while making a new, simpler shape.

concepts.name: 03-banked-f
concepts.title: Banked F
concepts.direction: Hybrid of curved enclosure and swept blades

Specific concept: BANKED F. Combine a rounded banked outer contour with an open aerodynamic F structure. A broad crescent-shaped left stem turns smoothly from the lower left into a long upper-right-facing airfoil; a shorter inner blade projects from the same curved spine toward the right. The space between these arms is a broad curved white wedge, and the underside stays open. The two arms and spine read as a single connected custom F, not a circle with a symbol inserted. Nearly square footprint, substantial lower-left curve, two purposeful rising terminals, softly rounded interior joins, crisp outer tips. This hybrid should sit midway between the sharp open first reference and the rounded compact second reference. Avoid a literal feather, bird head, letter G or generic swoosh.
